subject: Climate & Environment
title: Biodiversity Hotspots
description: Learn Biodiversity Hotspots in one minute.

hook.text: 36 regions hold over half of all plant species on Earth — on just 2.5% of the land.

buildup.text: These hotspots include Madagascar, the Andes, and the Philippines — all species-rich.

discovery.text: To qualify as a hotspot, a region must have at least 1,500 unique plant species and have lost 70% of habitat.

twist.text: Protecting just these 36 areas would safeguard a disproportionate share of global life.

climax.text: Most hotspots are in developing nations that lack funds for conservation.

punchline.text: Life concentrates in a few places. Losing them means losing everything.

quiz.question: How much of Earth's land do biodiversity hotspots cover?

details.summary: Biodiversity hotspots are regions that contain at least 1,500 endemic plant species while having lost at least 70 percent of their original habitat. The 36 recognized hotspots cover just 2.5 percent of Earth's land but hold over half its endemic plant species.
details.whyItMatters: Hotspots concentrate the most irreplaceable species in the smallest, most threatened areas. Protecting them delivers the greatest conservation return per dollar spent.
takeaways: 36 hotspots contain over 50 percent of endemic plant species
They cover only 2.5 percent of Earth's land surface
Over 70 percent of original habitat in each hotspot has been lost

faq.question: Which biodiversity hotspot has the most species?
faq.answer: The Tropical Andes hotspot is the richest on Earth, hosting about one-sixth of all plant species in the world, along with exceptional bird, amphibian, and mammal diversity. Much of its habitat is under threat from agriculture and mining.

faq.question: Who defined biodiversity hotspots and when?
faq.answer: British ecologist Norman Myers first identified 10 hotspots in 1988 based on endemic plant richness and habitat loss. Conservation International expanded and refined the concept, now recognizing 36 hotspots worldwide.
